advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `rebar fsck-recover` can actually remediate a DIVERGED (unrelated-history / non-ff) tracker; if not, adjust the DIVERGED hint to point at the true recovery path.
evidence: fsck.py:406-407 message: "Recover: run `rebar fsck-recover`, or re-clone and re-init"
fsck_recover.py:3-6 docstring: 'Detects a paused rebase/merge in the tracker worktree ... tries `git rebase --continue` ... on failure aborts + cherry-picks dangling `ticket: <EVENT> <id>` commits'
fsck_recover.py:65-74 _detect_stale_rebase only returns non-empty for rebase-merge/rebase-apply/REBASE_HEAD/MERGE_HEAD; a diverged-but-not-mid-rebase store yields '' -> nothing to do
Mitigating: _store/sync.py:145 already uses the same hint ('run: rebar fsck (then rebar fsck-recover)'), so this is an existing convention rather than newly introduced
advisory.finding: The DIVERGED recovery hint 'run `rebar fsck-recover`, or re-clone and re-init' may be misleading: fsck-recover only recovers from stale/interrupted rebase-merge state (dangling ticket commits), not from an unrelated-history or non-fast-forward divergence against origin/tickets. For a truly diverged store it detects no stale rebase and exits 0 ('nothing to do'), so it cannot heal the state this message reports.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving `fsck_cli(["--output", "json"])` (or `rebar fsck --output json`) against a divergent tracker asserting `payload["issue_count"] == 1` and an `issues[]` entry with `kind == "diverged"`.
evidence: fsck.py:196-200 makes DIVERGED increment `issue_count`, which feeds the JSON `issue_count`/`issues[]` payload (fsck.py:464 `payload = {"issues": issues, ... "issue_count": len(issues)}`).

The DIVERGED detail contains a ' — ' em-dash (fsck.py:402-408) that `_transform_json` partitions on (fsck.py:453 `head, sep, detail = rest.partition(" — ")`); `diverged` is NOT in `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` (fsck.py:50-58), so the JSON derivation path is untested for this new kind.

The JSON issue-accounting surface is an established, tested contract for fsck: tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_ensures.py:69-78 pins informational lines to `issue_count == 0` under `--output json`, but no analogous assertion exists for DIVERGED yielding `issue_count == 1` / `kind == "diverged"`.

ABSENCE: both new DIVERGED tests (test_fsck_push_pending.py:110-134 and :137-176) assert only text output (`"DIVERGED" in out`), exit code, and the classifier tuple — none drive `fsck_cli(["--output", "json"])` and parse the payload.
dropped.finding: The new DIVERGED counted-issue behavior is verified only in text mode and via the direct classifier tuple; no test exercises fsck's `--output json` surface for DIVERGED, so a regression in `_transform_json` (its `^([A-Z_]+):` regex or the ' — ' em-dash partition / `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` handling) could drop or misparse the counted DIVERGED issue in `issues[]`/`issue_count` with no test catching it.
scenarios: A future refactor of `_transform_json`'s regex or partition logic silently drops the DIVERGED line from `issues[]`, so `rebar fsck --output json` reports `issue_count: 0` for a divergent store while the JSON consumer (CI / operator tooling) sees 'no issues' — reintroducing the exact bug 01e8 symptom on the machine-readable surface.
dropped.suggested_fix: In tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_push_pending.py, after building the unrelated-history divergent tracker, call `fsck_mod.fsck_cli(["--output", "json"], repo_root=str(repo))`, `json.loads` the captured stdout, and assert `payload["issue_count"] == 1` and any(i["kind"] == "diverged" for i in payload["issues"]).
